hardware.name: Apple M1 Pro [cpu-numpy-blas-float32] calibrated
hardware.source: measured microbenchmarks on this host (NumPy/Accelerate BLAS); not a nominal GPU ceiling
hardware.notes: Effective profile for the CPU reference backend only.

assumptions: Dense decoder-only transformer with pre-norm blocks, no biases, and no positional-embedding table (RoPE assumed).
Linear-layer FLOPs use 2*weights*tokens (one multiply-add = 2 FLOPs). Embedding lookups and norm/elementwise FLOPs are ignored.
Attention FLOPs count QK^T and AV only. Causal prefill uses the exact triangular pair count; decode is non-causal because one query sees the whole context.
Weights are streamed once per forward (prefill) or once per decode step. No weight reuse across batches beyond that single stream.
KV-cache traffic is 2 (K and V) * layers * batch * context * kv_heads * head_dim * kv_bytes. Prefill writes and reads the new KV; decode reads the existing cache and writes one new token.
Activation traffic is a heuristic: activation_traffic_factor * layers * batch * tokens * hidden * activation_bytes. Set the factor to 0 for the core (weights + KV) byte count.
If attention_impl='materialized', the prefill/decode score matrix is written and read once: 2 * batch * heads * query_len * key_len * activation_bytes. 'fused' models a FlashAttention-style kernel.
Predicted latency = max(compute time, memory time) + per-layer launch overhead. It is an idealized lower bound when overhead is zero.
Nominal hardware peaks are datasheet/spec ceilings, not measured throughput. For measured CPU validation a calibrated hardware profile is supplied explicitly.

Predicted latency = max(compute time, memory time) + per-layer launch overhead. It is an idealized lower bound when overhead is zero.
Nominal hardware peaks are datasheet/spec ceilings, not measured throughput. For measured CPU validation a calibrated hardware profile is supplied explicitly.
